messages.content:
The issue is in the `FastDateFormat` class, specifically in the `getDateInstance` method. The `getDateInstance` method is responsible for creating instances of `FastDateFormat` based on the specified style, time zone, and locale.

From the failing test and the bug report, it seems that the `getDateInstance` method assumes that `Locale.getDefault()` won't change during its execution. The bug report mentions that if the default locale is changed after creating a `FastDateFormat` instance without specifying a locale, the wrong locale is applied.

Looking at the code snippet of the `FastDateFormat.getDateInstance` method, we can see that if the `locale` parameter is `null`, the method falls back to using the default locale by calling `Locale.getDefault()`. If the default locale is changed after creating an instance, it will not reflect the change and will continue to use the previously set default locale.

To fix this issue, the `getDateInstance` method should capture the default locale at the time of its invocation when `locale` is `null`, rather than retrieving it every time from `Locale.getDefault()`.

Next, I will suggest the methods that should be fixed to address this issue.
The methods that should be fixed to address this issue are:
```
org.apache.commons.lang.time.FastDateFormat.getDateInstance(int, java.util.Locale)
org.apache.commons.lang.time.FastDateFormat.getDateInstance(int, java.util.TimeZone, java.util.Locale)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
